items.criterion: The published version's search index is served from the object it was written into at publish, and the draft version has none to serve.
items.judgment: Fetch the index for the published version and for the draft, and read the bucket for both keys.

items.criterion: Walking the pager from the first page visits every page of the published version in flattened order.
items.judgment: Follow the next page from the first page and compare the walk against the stored sequence.

items.criterion: The flattened position of the published version runs from one to the page count with no gap and no duplicate.
items.judgment: Read every page row in flattened order and compare against the module and page order.

items.criterion: A draft whose internal link targets nothing fails validation and leaves the current version untouched.
items.judgment: Run the validation, read which check failed, attempt the publish, and re-read the current version.

items.criterion: The engine itself holds at most one current version rather than leaving the rule to application code.
items.judgment: Read the indexes, constraints and triggers on the version table.

items.criterion: A confirmation token moves a subscriber to confirmed once, and a second use reports the address as already confirmed.
items.judgment: Deliver the queued confirmation, open the link twice, and read the subscriber row between the two.

items.criterion: Many simultaneous submissions of one address leave one subscriber row and one queued message.
items.judgment: Submit in parallel and count the rows and the outbox entries afterwards.

items.criterion: An address already on a list is thanked rather than corrected, so the form cannot be probed for membership.
items.judgment: Submit a known address and read the response body for any admission that the address is known.

items.criterion: A mail callback carrying an invalid signature changes no subscriber state.
items.judgment: Post an unsigned callback and re-read the subscriber row and the recorded events.

items.criterion: A late delivery event cannot undo a complaint that arrived before the delivery.
items.judgment: Apply the two events out of order and read the final subscriber state.

items.criterion: Two simultaneous runs of one scheduled job leave at most one running, the other refused.
items.judgment: Start both runs together and read the job run rows and their locks.

items.criterion: The expiry sweep counts what would be deleted and refuses when the count is past its threshold.
items.judgment: Run the sweep and read the reported count against the stated threshold.

items.criterion: With the roster source unavailable the sponsor wall serves the last good roster with its age recorded.
items.judgment: Turn the source off, run the sync, and compare the served wall against the wall before.

items.criterion: A signed-out caller reaches no part of the draft version by any address.
items.judgment: Ask for the draft page, the draft tree and the preview address without a session.

items.criterion: Every studio address refuses a signed-out caller and serves none of the protected content.
items.judgment: Ask for each studio address without a session and read the status and the body.

items.criterion: With non-essential storage refused, a page view writes no row.
items.judgment: Record the refusal, fetch a page, and count the page-view rows before and after.

items.criterion: A call name that appears only inside a code specimen resolves to its page through the published index.
items.judgment: Read the index for the term and confirm the term is absent from every title.

items.criterion: Every sponsor mark and the roster document live as first-party objects at the pinned keys.
items.judgment: Read the bucket for each mark key and for the roster key.
